nodes.label: Three OAuth Clients Requirement
nodes.rationale: Android (package + SHA-1), iOS (bundle ID) and Web (origins + redirect URIs) clients are all needed; a single Web client cannot serve a mobile app. A custom scheme like uzcasting:// is rejected by the Web client's redirect URIs — native client types exist precisely because their redirect is derived from the package/bundle ID.

nodes.label: Shared Debug Keystore For EAS
nodes.rationale: EAS would otherwise generate its own keystore, producing a second SHA-1 that would have to be added to the Android client; instead the debug keystore is copied into mobile/credentials and wired via credentials.json with credentialsSource: local. The release SHA-1 (or the Play App Signing re-issued key) must be added before production login works.

nodes.label: Dual URL Scheme In app.json
nodes.rationale: expo-auth-session builds a native redirect of uz.uzcasting.app:/oauthredirect, which is not the primary 'uzcasting' scheme, so both are registered; without the second the browser could not return to the app after consent and login would hang on a blank tab. For web preview, Google additionally requires the exact origin (e.g. http://localhost:8082) or it returns redirect_uri_mismatch.

nodes.label: app.google.client-ids Server Property
nodes.rationale: POST /api/v1/auth/google validates the ID token against an allowlist of client IDs and deliberately answers 503 when the list is missing rather than accepting any token. All client IDs must be listed because each platform's token carries its own aud.

nodes.label: Google Login Deploy Blockers
nodes.rationale: Remaining blockers are the backend deploy and then the client-ids property, in that order. A curl probe distinguishes them: 405 means the old build is deployed (Spring Boot's static handler answers GET-only on /**), 503 means the property is unset, 401 means everything is configured.

nodes.label: expo-auth-session Over Native SDK
nodes.rationale: Browser OAuth with no native modules was chosen because it needs nothing but a client ID and can later be swapped for @react-native-google-signin without rewriting screens — everything is hidden behind GoogleSignInButton. Two traps hit already: Google.useIdTokenAuthRequest throws without a client ID (hooks cannot be called conditionally, so the button mounts only when keys exist), and the import path must be lowercase 'google' or Metro fails on non-Windows filesystems.

nodes.label: .env Does Not Reach EAS Builds
nodes.rationale: EAS uploads only git-tracked files and .env is gitignored, so every EXPO_PUBLIC_* would be undefined in the APK with no build error — visible only on the phone. Client IDs are therefore duplicated into eas.json env for the development and preview profiles (no secrets: a client ID ships inside the APK anyway). eas.json also rejects '//' comment keys.

nodes.label: Phone-Or-Google Auth Flow
nodes.rationale: Agreed with the client: sign in by phone OR Google. Requiring a phone after Google turned out to be our own invention, not a TZ requirement, so the backend's phone_required is now a hint that the account has no number rather than a block; the number is requested only where it is genuinely needed (creator payouts, phone-bound payment systems). The (auth)/phone-link screen remains but is opened on demand with a 'later' option.
